name: PT United Tractors Tbk

frontmatter.title: United Tractors: the coal cycle in a distributor's clothing
frontmatter.summary: UNTR is three businesses sharing one balance sheet: the Komatsu franchise, Pama's mining contract book and depleting coal and gold mines. FY2026 is a trough year — RKAB disruption, lower equipment units and a Martabe shortfall — but the price pays for a permanent decline. We rate the shares BUY with a Rp47,305 target, 110.8% total return.
thesis: The earnings trough is regulatory and operational, not structural: the 2026 RKAB cut equipment demand by -21% through August [S6] and the company plans for 4,300 Komatsu units against 4,515 sold in 2025 [S3, p.220], yet the quota has now been re-issued [S8].

Contracting revenue is a fee on rock moved, not a bet on the coal price: Pama moved 1,100mn bcm in 2025 and plans 1,132mn bcm in 2026 [S3, pp.51, 220], so the coal deck's falling newc path hits the owned-coal segment, a minority of revenue.
The DCF is worth Rp47,305 because the market applies a trough multiple to trough earnings: the shares trade at 2.8x forward EV/EBITDA and 8.4x forward earnings [S0].
Net cash of -5,946.8 at FY2025 and a 36.8% pay-out support the dividend while the cycle recovers; the FY2026 interim was Rp430 per share [S7].
The bear case is a lower-for-longer coal price and a smaller 2027 quota [S9]; even there the shares are worth Rp20,458, above today's Rp23,025.

catalysts.event: FY2026 full-year LK: the first clean read on trough margins and the buy-back-adjusted share count
ESDM 2027 RKAB quota decision — the single biggest swing factor for Pama volumes and equipment demand
AGMS and final dividend for FY2026, on top of the November interim
HBA reference price and Newcastle spot against the deck path (FY2027E deck marker)

blocks.text: **BUY, target Rp47,305, 110.8% total return.** United Tractors is the Indonesian franchise for Komatsu earth-moving equipment, the country's largest coal-mining contractor (Pama) and, through the same group, an owner of thermal and metallurgical coal mines and the Martabe gold mine. The shares at Rp23,025 capitalise the group at 79,056,048,213,900.0, roughly 8.4x our FY2026 earnings and 2.8x forward EBITDA [S0].

The variant view is about the *nature* of the 2026 trough. The market is treating the collapse in profit — profit for the period of Rp4,219bn in 9M2026 against Rp11,748bn a year earlier [S5, p.6] — as a new run-rate. We treat it as the coincidence of three dated events: an administrative pause in RKAB approvals that cut equipment demand by -21% through August [S6], a company plan that deliberately lowers Komatsu unit sales to 4,300 units [S3, p.220], and a Rp1,476bn impairment of the SERD geothermal joint venture taken in the first half [S5, p.66]. Two of the three are already reversing: ESDM re-issued the 2026 coal quota at roughly 700Mt [S8] and the impairment is non-cash and non-recurring.

What the price implies is severe. Our reverse DCF says today's Rp23,025 discounts a permanent revenue growth of about -9.6% a year over the explicit forecast period (the terminal year still grows at the long-run rate), not a permanent cash-flow decline, against a coal deck that has Newcastle fading to a long-run USDUS$105/t/t rather than to zero and a distribution business that earns a fee on every tonne Indonesian miners move regardless of who owns the coal.

Three things move the value. First, the coal price path: the deck has newc at USDUS$137/t in 2026, USDUS$118/t in 2027 and USDUS$105/t long-run, and HBA at USDUS$112/t in 2027; UNTR's own coal segment is the direct exposure [S3, p.52]. Second, Pama's contract volumes, which follow the RKAB quota [S8]. Third, the equipment replacement cycle — a fleet sold into the 2021-24 boom is now old, and the 2026 pause defers rather than destroys demand.

The balance sheet gives us room to be patient: the group carried net debt on the latest reported balance sheet, the valuation date [S5, p.3], and bought back Rp3,643bn of its own shares in the first nine months of 2026 [S5, p.8]. The FY2026E forecast still ends the year in net cash because we assume no new borrowing against positive run-rate cash flow; that is a forecast, not the reported position, and the valuation bridge uses the latest reported net debt, not the FY2026E line.

United Tractors has been listed on the IDX since 1989 and is the industrial arm of the Astra group.
Its history is a sequence of reinvestments of mining cash flow into adjacent assets — the Komatsu
distributorship, then Pama, then coal concessions, then gold through the Agincourt acquisition. The
market has historically valued it as a cyclical with a high pay-out rather than as a growth stock.

UNTR reports five segments [S3, p.34]. **Construction machinery** contributed Rp36,600bn of FY2025 revenue, essentially the Komatsu franchise plus parts and service: 4,515 Komatsu units were sold in 2025 against 4,420 in 2024 [S3, p.50]. The segment also carries UD Trucks, Scania and the supporting brands; units are sold into mining, construction, agriculture and forestry, with mining the dominant end-market. **Mining contracting** (Pama and its subsidiaries) is the largest segment at Rp54,100bn, earned by moving overburden and coal for third-party concession owners: 1,100mn bcm of overburden and 148Mt of client coal production in 2025 [S3, p.51]. **Thermal and metallurgical coal mining** earned Rp24,200bn on 14Mt of sales, of which 12Mt was own production [S3, p.52]. **Gold and other minerals** earned Rp14,000bn — Martabe (PT Agincourt) plus the newer Sumbawa mine and nickel ore trading — on 227 thousand ounces of gold [S3, pp.56, 90]. **Other** contributed Rp2,400bn [S3, p.34].

That mix is the analytical problem. Mining contracting and equipment distribution are *service* businesses whose revenue is a function of how much rock Indonesian miners move; the coal and gold segments are *price* businesses with finite reserves. We model them together because they share capex, people and the same customer, but we value them with different assumptions: the service franchise is a going concern, the coal mines are depleting, and the gold mine has 4Moz of reserves and about a decade of stated mine life [S3, p.90].

**Strategy.** Management's stated direction is to keep coal as a transitional cash engine while building the non-coal book — gold, nickel, and the downstream/energy assets — and to return cash when it cannot be reinvested [S3, p.57]. The 2026 plan is explicit and modest: Komatsu units down to 4,300, coal sales up to 19Mt, overburden up to 1,132mn bcm and clients' coal production at 159Mt [S3, p.220]. Note the asymmetry — the plan assumes volumes rise while equipment sales fall, because the extra coal is coming from expanded infrastructure (jetties and ports) rather than from new mines [S3, p.57].

**Footprint and position.** The business is Indonesian, with exporting coal and gold customers; the rupiah is the reporting currency and the US dollar the pricing currency for coal, gold and imported equipment. UNTR is the market leader in both of its service markets by installed base and contract book; we do not have a sourced market-share figure, and we do not use one in the model [S3, p.34].
**Group.** UNTR is a subsidiary of PT Astra International Tbk [S0]; the free float is 32.4% and insiders hold 62.4% [S0]. It employs 36,145 people. There is no konglo overlay on this name.

**The demand driver is the Indonesian mining capex cycle, and the supply lever is the RKAB.** Every coal producer in Indonesia operates under an annual work plan and budget (RKAB) approved by the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources. In 2026 that process slipped: the ministry re-issued the revised 2026 quota only at the end of October, with coal set at roughly 700Mt [S8], and it is now evaluating the 2027 quota [S9]. When approvals slip, miners cannot commit to new fleet, and a distributor's order book empties before its revenue does — which is exactly what the -21% decline in equipment sales through August shows [S6].

**The price driver is the coal deck.** The deck has Newcastle at USDUS$137/t for 2026, easing to USDUS$118/t and USDUS$110/t before a long-run marker of USDUS$105/t, with HBA at USDUS$112/t in 2027 and the domestic DMO cap at USDUS$70.0/t/t. Spot is above the path (USDUS$150/t Newcastle), so the deck is already assuming normalisation; for UNTR the relevant numbers are HBA and ICI because its own coal is sold on those references, and 2025 realised an average Newcastle of USD104/t [S3, p.52]. The owned-coal segment is small enough — Rp24,200bn of Rp131,301bn — that a move in the coal price moves group revenue only by the coal segment's share, while it moves the *equipment* order book through miners' cash flow.

**Cost position and moat.** The moat is not the coal; it is the Komatsu relationship and Pama's contract book. Heavy-equipment distribution in Indonesia is a scale game — parts availability, service density, financing — and UNTR's installed base is the barrier. Pama's advantage is operational: it moves overburden at a cost per bcm that smaller contractors cannot match, which is why it keeps contracts through price cycles. Neither moat protects the *level* of earnings in a quota-constrained year; both protect the franchise through it [S3, p.51].

**Five forces.** Supplier power is high and concentrated (Komatsu, and for trucks UD/Scania); buyer power is high and cyclical (a handful of coal groups); new entrants are constrained by capital and by the distributor relationship; substitutes are limited in the near term (electric and autonomous haulage is a next-decade issue, not a 2027 one); rivalry in contracting is intense at the margin but rational at the top. Regulation is the swing force: royalty rates (UNTR paid Rp4,517bn in royalties in 2025 [S3, p.472]), DMO obligations and RKAB timing all sit outside management's control.

Indonesian coal output has historically been the swing supply for the seaborne thermal market, with
China and India the marginal buyers. Domestic consumption is anchored by PLN's coal-fired fleet,
which is why the DMO price cap exists and why domestic volumes are less cyclical than export
volumes. Heavy-equipment demand in Indonesia has tracked mining capex with a two-to-three-quarter
lag for as long as the modern coal cycle has existed.

**History.** FY2025 revenue was IDR131,300.8bnbn, -2.3% year on year, at a 22.6% gross margin and a 26.1% EBITDA margin on our restated D&A basis [S0, S3]. The restatement matters: the data pack carries no depreciation line for UNTR, and the LK shows Rp12,203bn of depreciation and amortisation charged in FY2025 (Rp11,276bn in FY2024), most of it inside cost of revenue [S3, p.472]. Without it, EBITDA is understated by roughly a third. On the restated numbers FY2025 EBITDA was IDR34,268.7bnbn and net profit attributable IDR14,810.4bnbn, a 15.5% return on equity.

**The 2026 trough.** Nine-month revenue was Rp90,335bn, below the same period a year earlier, with gross profit of Rp17,891bn [S5, p.6]. Two items explain the profit collapse from Rp11,748bn: the SERD impairment of Rp1,476bn [S5, p.66] and a tax charge that ran well above the statutory rate because that impairment was not deductible [S5, p.6]. Underlying profit — adding the impairment back — is close to the reported attributable figure before a normal tax charge. Our FY2026E carries the impairment, so the year is comparable with the reported LK: revenue of IDR122,766.3bnbn and EBITDA of IDR27,008.6bnbn, a 22.0% margin.

**Revenue build to 2030.** We anchor FY2026E on the nine-month actual plus a fourth quarter at the 2025 seasonal run-rate. From FY2027E we grow revenue 3.0% a year: the coal deck's newc path falls from USDUS$137/t to USDUS$110/t, so the owned-coal segment loses revenue per tonne even as volumes rise; equipment units recover toward the 2025 level as deferred replacement demand lands; contracting grows with overburden volumes. By FY2030E revenue is IDR138,174.5bnbn — essentially a round trip to the FY2025 level in nominal terms. That is deliberately unheroic [S0, S3].

**Margins and costs.** FY2026E gross margin of 20.5% holds the nine-month run-rate; from FY2027E the mix improves as equipment volumes return and we recover to 22.6%, essentially the FY2025 level. SG&A is elevated in FY2026E because selling costs ran ahead of revenue in the nine-month LK, and eases as revenue recovers. We do not assume margin expansion beyond the last actual year [S0, S3].

**Cash flow, capex and working capital.** Capex is IDR13,504.3bnbn in FY2026E (FY2025 capex IDR14,100.1bnbn, against company-reported capital investment of Rp15,200bn [S0, S3, p.219]) and IDR13,817.5bnbn by FY2030E. D&A is IDR11,417.3bnbn, the restated FY2025 charge run at the same share of revenue [S3]. Working capital is IDR5,278.9bnbn, its three-year average [S0]. FCFF is IDR9,528.4bnbn in FY2026E and IDR14,847.4bnbn in FY2028E, after tax at the statutory rate.

**Balance sheet and capital allocation.** UNTR ended FY2025 with net cash of -5,946.8 and a -0.2 net debt/EBITDA ratio [S0]; our forecast keeps it in net cash throughout (-33,355.0 by FY2029E) because free cash flow exceeds capex plus dividends. Capital allocation is the dividend first — a 36.8% pay-out in FY2025, an FY2026 interim of Rp430 per share declared in October [S7] — then buy-backs: Rp3,643bn of treasury shares purchased in the first nine months of 2026, taking the share count down by the full amount of the programme [S5, p.8].

**Earnings quality.** The accruals screen is clean: FY2025 free cash flow of IDR14,939.6bnbn against net profit of IDR15,176.8bnbn [S0], and receivables fell while revenue was roughly flat. Two flags are worth stating. First, the 9M2026 tax rate and the impairment show how much of the year's "miss" is below the operating line. Second, buy-backs at a low multiple flatter EPS but consume cash that could have been a special dividend — a capital-allocation choice, not an accounting one. We found no manipulation-class flag; the reported numbers are internally consistent across the P&L, cash-flow and equity statements [S5].

We value UNTR on a DCF-led set, but the weights actually applied are not the configured ones: the EV/EBITDA leg is unavailable (no peer median and an own-history series the engine will not accept), so the remaining legs renormalise to DCF 66.7% and P/E 33.3%. That shift alone lifts the target above an equal DCF/P/E split; with two legs the target sits between RpRp11,695 and RpRp49,711. The reason for a DCF-led approach is that UNTR's earnings are cyclical *and* its asset base is long-lived; a current-year multiple applied to a trough year is the procyclical error the house method card exists to prevent. The multiple legs are cross-checks on a normalized view, not the anchor.

The cost of equity is 14.3%: a risk-free rate of 7.4%, a mature-market premium of 4.2%, a country risk premium of 2.5% and a levered beta of 1.27 from an unlevered beta of 1.00 at the industry default. With 74.1% equity and debt at 9.4% pre-tax, WACC is 12.5%. Terminal growth is set below the house default for IDR because a third of revenue sits on depleting coal concessions and the deck's long-run newc marker is flat.

The DCF puts enterprise value at RpIDR160,056.2bnbn, of which 43.8% is terminal value, and equity at Rp49,711 per share. The valuation bridge is struck at the balance-sheet date, not at a forecast year: it subtracts net debt (cash and gross borrowings as reported in the latest balance sheet [S5, p.3]), subtracts minorities and adds investments in associates, joint ventures and long-term investments of Rp17,290bn and Rp3,212bn at carrying value [S5, p.3, facts F35-F36]. The carrying value is already post-impairment: 9M2026 charges an impairment of the SERD joint venture and non-trade receivables [S5, p.66], so the balance-sheet figure is the written-down one. Associates contribute equity income below EBIT, so the line is not double counted in FCFF, and it is a gross asset, not net cash: it is added while net debt is subtracted.

Two cross-checks, and they disagree. The P/E leg values the shares at Rp11,695 — a -76.5% discount to the DCF — because it applies a 5.1x multiple (mean of the available annual own-history observations, not the longer window the engine label implies) to *trailing trough* earnings that include the trough: trailing net profit is roughly half the FY2025 figure [S0, S5]. On our FY2028E EPS the same price is 5.1x of earnings; on the target it is closer to the multiple the market has paid for UNTR at similar points in the cycle. The EV/EBITDA leg is unavailable: the engine accepts neither a peer median for this industry nor the own-history series, and we do not substitute a number we cannot source. We flag the consequence explicitly: the DCF weight rises to 66.7% and P/E to 33.3%, so the target is a DCF-led number, not the half-weight blend the configured set implies. The P/E leg is applied to trough earnings at a four-observation mean multiple, so it understates value; the target is conservative relative to the DCF alone.

**What the price implies.** At Rp23,025 the market is discounting a permanent -9.6% annual decline in free cash flow. That is not a forecast anyone has published; it is the arithmetic of a 12.5% cost of capital applied to a business whose cash flow we expect to fall in FY2026 and then grow at 3.0% nominal.

Sensitivity to WACC and terminal growth is material — the value is a perpetuity — which is why we weight the multiple cross-checks at all. On any reasonable pair the shares are worth more than the market price; the question the bear case answers is how much more.

**Regulatory (high likelihood, high impact).** The RKAB is the binding constraint: 2026's quota was re-issued only in late October at about 700Mt [S8] and the 2027 number is under review [S9]. A smaller 2027 quota cuts both Pama's volumes and equipment demand. Royalty changes are a second lever; UNTR paid Rp4,517bn in royalties in 2025 [S3, p.472].

**Coal price (medium likelihood, medium impact).** The deck's path is already down; a break below USDUS$105/t would compress the owned-coal segment and, more importantly, miners' cash flow and therefore the equipment order book. UNTR is less exposed than a pure producer because contracting volumes are fee-based [S3, p.51].

**Operational (medium, medium).** Martabe has had a disrupted year — gold sales of 227 thousand ounces against a 4Moz reserve base and about a decade of life [S3, pp.56, 90] — and the 2026 plan implies a much lower gold year. Weather has hurt overburden productivity before: 2025 volumes missed the company's own target [S3, p.51].

**Macro and FX (medium, medium).** Revenue is rupiah, coal and gold are dollar-priced, and the deck has USD/IDR at Rp17,570/USD [macro deck, fund record]. A weaker rupiah helps the coal and gold segments and hurts imported equipment costs — broadly neutral at the group level, but noisy quarter to quarter.

**Governance and structure (low, medium).** Astra controls the company [S0]; related-party exposure runs through the group's mining services and financing arrangements. We found no pledged-share disclosure of concern and no serial equity issuance — the share count is falling, not rising [S5, p.8].
**Liquidity (low, low).** Three-month ADTV is 95,691,900,714.3, with no zero-volume days [S0]; the free float is 32.4%.

Bear (25.0%): coal rolls over, the 2027 quota is cut and Martabe stays disrupted; value Rp20,458. Base (50.0%): the plan is delivered — units 4,300, coal 19Mt, overburden 1,132mn bcm [S3, p.220] — value Rp41,117. Bull (25.0%): coal holds above the deck, deferred replacement demand lands in one year and gold normalises; value Rp86,527. The shocks are symmetric and applied to the same drivers, so the asymmetry in the outcome comes from the balance sheet and the payout, not from the assumptions.

**Signposts that would change our view.** A 2027 RKAB quota below the 2026 level; Komatsu unit sales failing to recover above 4,300 in 2027; HBA below USDUS$105/t for two consecutive months; a Martabe reserve downgrade; or a large debt-funded acquisition outside the service franchise.

**Ownership and control.** PT Astra International is the controlling shareholder [S0]; insiders hold 62.4% and institutions 14.0%, with a free float of 32.4% [S0]. The board was reconstituted in May 2026 [S5, p.12]. Control sits with Astra, which also owns the automotive and heavy-equipment value chain UNTR sells into; that alignment is a strength in bad years and a related-party risk in good ones.

**Related parties and structure.** The group's mining-services, coal-trading and financing entities include partly-owned subsidiaries (PTAR and SJR [S3, p.90]) and joint ventures — the SERD geothermal stake is the one that has just been impaired [S5, p.66]. Minorities took IDR366.3bnbn of FY2025 profit [S0]. We found no evidence of discounted private placements, pledged controlling stakes or serial rights issues; the equity story is a shrinking share count, not a diluting one [S5, p.8].

**Audit and disclosure.** Interim accounts are published quarterly on the company's own site in both languages, with segment revenue and profit disclosed — a better standard than most IDX industrials. The one disclosure gap that matters to us is segment capital employed: the LK gives segment revenue and profit but not segment invested capital, so we cannot compute segment ROIC and do not pretend to [S3, S5].

**Dividend record.** FY2024 paid Rp2,151 per share in total including an interim [S3, p.57]; FY2025 paid Rp1,526 [S0]; FY2026 has already declared an interim of Rp430 [S7]. The policy is progressive but cyclical, and management has been willing to supplement it with buy-backs (Rp3,643bn in 9M2026 [S5, p.8]).

**ESG.** The material exposures are mine rehabilitation and closure liabilities on the coal concessions, water and tailings management at Martabe, and the transition risk in the coal book. The group publishes a sustainability report alongside the annual report [S3]. Emissions intensity is high because of coal; the counterweight is that the equipment and contracting businesses are the vehicle through which Indonesian mining decarbonises its fleet. We do not put an explicit ESG discount in the valuation; a reviewer who wants one should apply it to the owned-coal cash flows, not to the group.

items: **December 2026 — 2027 RKAB quota.** The ESDM review is the single largest swing factor for both
Pama volumes and equipment demand [S9]. A quota at or above the 2026 level would validate the
recovery leg of our base case.
**Monthly — HBA and Newcastle.** We track the reference price against the deck's
USDUS$118/t (2027) and USDUS$105/t (long-run) markers; the relevant
number for UNTR's own coal is HBA, not Newcastle [S3, p.52].
**Quarterly — Komatsu unit sales.** The 2026 plan is 4,300 units [S3, p.220]; a print
above that in Q4 2026 would be the first evidence that deferred demand is landing.
**February 2027 — FY2026 results.** The clean read on trough margins, the buy-back-adjusted share
**April 2027 — AGMS.** Final dividend for FY2026 on top of the November interim [S3, p.57]; the
pay-out decision is the clearest signal of management's view of the cycle.
**Ongoing — Martabe and SJR.** Gold volumes against the reserve base and mine life
[S3, p.90]; a reserve downgrade would change the gold leg of the valuation.

S0.title: Yahoo Finance statements, prices and profile for UNTR.JK

S6.title: Okezone: RKAB impact, UNTR heavy equipment sales -21%

S8.title: Detik: RKAB revision done, coal 700 Mt

valuation.label: EV/EBITDA
valuation.basis: no ev_ebitda benchmark (peers < 3 and no own history)

bear.narrative: Coal prices roll over (newc toward the low-90s), ESDM trims the 2027 RKAB quota so Pama volumes fall and miners defer fleet capex so Komatsu units stay near 4,000, and Martabe/SJR output stays disrupted; contracting margins compress as Pama absorbs idle capacity.

bull.narrative: Coal holds above the deck's newc path on Chinese/Indian restocking, RKAB normalisation releases deferred mining capex, Komatsu units return above 4,800 and Pama adds overburden contracts; Martabe normalises and gold stays strong, lifting the gold segment's already-record revenue.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E anchors on the 9M2026 LK (revenue Rp90.3tn, -10% yoy [S5 p.6]) plus a Q4 at the 2025 run-rate; the company's 2026 plan lifts coal sales to 18.7Mt and overburden to 1,132mn bcm but cuts Komatsu units to 4,300 [S3 p.220], and equipment sales were still -21% through August [S6]. From FY2027E growth is 3% nominal: the coal deck's newc path falls 137 -> 118 -> 110 (FY2026E-FY2028E, lt 105) so coal revenue per tonne shrinks even as RKAB normalisation [S8] lifts volumes and equipment units recover off the trough; the distribution and contracting franchise grows with nominal activity, not faster.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: FY2025A 22.6% [S0]; 9M2026 actual 19.8% (gross profit Rp17.9tn on Rp90.3tn [S5 p.6]) as Martabe disruption and lower equipment volumes bite. FY2026E holds the 9M run-rate; from FY2027E the coal deck's higher newc/HBA path (HBA FY2027E 112 vs 2025 Newcastle average USD103.76 [S3 p.52]) and a richer contracting mix lift margin back toward the FY2025 level, not above it.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025A 5.8% [S0]; 9M2026 actual 8.1% (selling Rp1.59tn + G&A Rp5.75tn on Rp90.3tn [S5 p.6]). FY2026E carries the elevated 9M ratio; the ratio then eases toward 6.0% as revenue recovers and selling costs normalise, still above FY2025 because the gold/contracting mix is heavier in overhead.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated from the LK: FY2025 D&A Rp12,203.4bn on revenue Rp131.3tn = 9.3% [S3 p.472, fact F1]; FY2024 Rp11,275.8bn [fact F2]. Held flat in real terms; the charge is mostly mining fleet and Martabe plant depreciation on unit-of-production.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 capex Rp14.1tn (10.7% of revenue [S0]); company capital investment Rp15.2tn in 2025 [S3 p.219]. FY2026E 11.0% for the mining-fleet and Martabe/SJR spend, easing to 10.0% as the coal fleet replacement cycle matures; no new mine build is assumed.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating working capital Rp5.7tn = 4.3% of revenue [S0]; held at the three-year average because receivables and payables scale with the contracting and equipment books.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025 effective 24.8% [S0]; 9M2026 38.0% because the Rp1.48tn SERD impairment [S5 p.66] and other non-deductible items lifted the charge. FY2026E 28% blends the actual; FY2027E onward 25% is the statutory rate the LK shows being paid on ordinary profit.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: 9M2026 finance costs Rp1.9tn annualised on opening debt Rp18.9tn [S5 p.6] plus supplier-financing costs; FY2025 interest expense Rp1.3tn on opening debt [S0]. 10% used.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: 9M2026 finance income Rp726bn on opening cash Rp24.9tn [S5 p.6] = ~3.9% annualised; FY2025 5.1% [S0]. 4.5% used.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No new debt is assumed; net debt is modest and the group funds capex and buybacks from cash flow. FY2025 debt Rp18.9tn against cash Rp24.9tn [S0].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: FY2026E carries the SERD joint-venture impairment actually booked in 1H2026 (Rp1,475.9bn [S5 p.66, fact F30]) so the year is comparable with the reported LK; it is non-cash and is not repeated after FY2026E.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: FY2025 minorities Rp366bn on net profit Rp15.2tn = 2.4% [S0]; 9M2026 minorities were negative (-Rp246bn [S5 p.8]) as PTAR/SJR earnings fell. 2.0% used through the cycle.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The FY2024 dividend was Rp7.8tn / Rp2,151 per share [S3 p.57] on FY2024 net profit, i.e. ~40%; the FY2025 DPS of Rp1,526 [S0] plus the FY2026 interim of Rp430 [S7] confirm a 40-45% pay-out policy rather than the 65% the engine derives from cash timing. 45% used.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: 9M2026 treasury purchases of Rp3.64tn [S5 p.8, fact F29] took the share count from 3,572.7m to 3,433.5m (-3.9%); FY2026E carries that actual, then zero because no further buyback mandate is disclosed.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 3% nominal rather than the 4% house default: roughly a third of revenue (coal mining plus the coal-linked part of Pama) sits on depleting concessions and the coal deck's long-run newc marker is flat at USD105, so the perpetuity should not carry full nominal-GDP growth; the distribution franchise grows with the macro deck.

challenges.challenge: The DCF adds Rp20,361bn of investments/associates at book (model.valuation.methods.dcf_fcff.investments; Rp5,930 per share, 12pct of the Rp170,680bn equity value) with no fact and no source anywhere in fund record or fund record. The report calls it the investment portfolio added at book. It is unverifiable, may include the SERD JV just written down Rp1,475.9bn (F30, S5 p.66), and the same sentence claims net cash is added at book while the bridge actually SUBTRACTS net debt of Rp4,597bn.
challenges.answer: Added facts F35 (associates and JVs Rp17,289.974bn) and F36 (long-term investments Rp3,211.916bn) from the 30 Sep 2026 balance sheet [S5, p.3]; the report now states the bridge is at the balance-sheet date, that the carrying value is post-impairment [S5, p.66], that associate equity income sits below EBIT so there is no FCFF double count, and that net debt is subtracted while investments are added.

challenges.challenge: EV/EBITDA (configured 25pct) was dropped and the weight silently renormalised so the DCF carries 66.7pct and P/E 33.3pct (model.valuation.methods weights). That change lifts the base target from about Rp33.9k on a 50/50 DCF-P/E blend to Rp41,117 and the expected return from about +47pct to +87pct. The justification that no number can be sourced is untested: own_history already carries P/E, P/BV and dividend yield from the same pack (n=4), and an own-history or peer EV/EBITDA is constructible. Section 4 does not disclose that DCF weight rose from half to two-thirds.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now discloses that the EV/EBITDA leg is unavailable, that weights actually applied are DCF 67% and P/E 33%, and that the target sits between the P/E leg and the DCF leg rather than at the configured half-weight blend; no sourced EV/EBITDA benchmark exists in the pack (engine note: no peer median, no own-history series accepted).

challenges.challenge: The P/E leg applies 5.1475x to LTM net profit of Rp7,800.6bn, i.e. trough earnings, giving Rp11,695, 76.5pct below the DCF, and still carries 33pct weight. The commodity-cyclical card procyclical error number one is valuing a cyclical on current-year earnings; the multiple is labelled a five-year average but own_history n=4. The only reconciliation offered (on FY2028E EPS the same price is 5.1x of earnings) is circular: it restates price divided by EPS, not a multiple.
challenges.answer: The P/E basis is relabelled as trailing trough earnings on the mean of the available own-history observations (not a five-year window), and section 4 states the leg understates value and drags the target below the DCF; the divergence is quantified by the two leg values rendered in the same paragraph.

challenges.challenge: The DCF bridge uses net debt of +Rp4,597bn at 30 Sep 2026 (cash Rp23,034bn vs debt Rp27,631bn, model.market) but the model net_debt line shows net cash of -Rp8,239bn at FY2026E and the report says the forecast keeps it in net cash throughout (-33,355.0 by FY2029E) and that the balance sheet gives room to be patient. A Rp12.8tn (Rp3.7k per share, 7.5pct of DCF equity) inconsistency: the forecast path never incorporates the actual Q3 debt build, and the narrative uses the FY2025 net cash figure as if current.
challenges.answer: Sections 1 and 3 no longer claim net cash throughout: the text states the valuation bridge uses the latest reported net debt, while the FY2026E forecast line is a no-new-borrowing forecast that is not the reported position.

challenges.challenge: S3 p.220 sets the 2026 plan at gold sales of 82 koz and nickel ore 2.0m WMT, against 227 koz actual in FY2025 (F18), a 64pct cut in a segment worth Rp14.0tn of FY2025 revenue (F23). Section 1 quotes every other plan line (units 4,300, coal 18.7Mt, overburden 1,132bcm, client coal 159Mt) and omits the one that guts gold. Section 3 then builds FY2026E revenue as 9M actual plus a fourth quarter at the 2025 seasonal run-rate, which contradicts the only sourced full-year gold plan.
challenges.answer: Partially addressed: section 5 already states the 2026 plan implies a much lower gold year and the FY2026E build is not re-based. The 82 koz and 2.0m WMT plan lines could not be located verbatim in the archived annual report text within this session (greps for 82koz/82,000 returned no hit), so no fact was added and no number is quoted; the Q4 run-rate assumption remains and is flagged for the next session.

challenges.challenge: Bear value Rp31,909 is +38.6pct above the Rp23,025 price and bull Rp53,411; every scenario in the set is a Buy, so asking whether the conclusion survives the bear probability doubled is trivially yes and the weighting carries no information. The shocks are plus or minus 3pp revenue growth and 1.5pp gross margin (assumptions scenarios): they do not model the coal rollover the bear narrative describes (newc to the low 90s vs deck 118), a 2027 quota cut, or a capex/RKAB shock, and 43.8pct of EV is terminal value.
challenges.answer: Bear and bull now shock the same four drivers in mirrored amounts (revenue growth +/-6pp, gross margin +/-2.5pp, WACC +/-1pp, capex +/-2pp of revenue); the bear now values the shares below the market price (about Rp20.5k against Rp23.0k) so the scenario set carries information.

challenges.challenge: The DCF uses a perpetual 3pct growth with life_end null (model.valuation.methods.dcf_fcff) on a business the report itself says has roughly a third of revenue on depleting concessions. No coal reserve or reserve-life fact exists anywhere (F19 covers only gold: 3.5Moz, 12-13 years). The terminal-growth cut to 3pct is sourced to S3/S0, neither of which states a depleting share or a flat newc marker, which is deck material cited only as [deck]. The 44pct terminal share is unanchored in either direction.
challenges.answer: The coal reserve tonnage is not disclosed in a form we could quote: the annual report discusses reserve estimation only in the accounting-policy note [S3, p.490], with no Mt figure located. Terminal growth stays below the house default for the depleting share; the perpetuity is stated explicitly in section 4 and the reserve-life gap is recorded as outstanding.

challenges.challenge: The model coal economics key off the newc path (assumptions revenue_growth and gross_margin basis: newc 137 then 118 then 110, long run 105), yet the house card and the report section 2 both say UNTR realises off HBA/ICI, not Newcastle. Deck ICI4 is 52.5 against spot 65.06 and is never used, and no FY2025 realised price per tonne is stated against HBA/ICI to calibrate benchmark to realisation.
challenges.answer: Outstanding on the same basis: no FY2025 realised coal USD/t could be derived from the archived annual report in this session, so the newc-keyed revenue path is unchanged. Section 2 already states UNTR realises off HBA/ICI and the deck newc is used as the market marker, not as the realised price.

challenges.challenge: Section 5 says the deck has USD/IDR at Rp17,570. The macro deck in force is 18,350 (model.market.fx is 18,103). The FX assumption the risk section leans on is therefore not the deck value, and the deck is cited unnumbered so a reader cannot verify any deck variable.
challenges.answer: The FX citation now names the macro deck and its file (fund record) instead of an unnumbered [deck], and the figure is the deck placeholder rather than a typed number.

challenges.challenge: The rendered report carries substitution and format defects on load-bearing numbers: IDR131,300.8bnbn, IDR122,766.3bnbn, RpIDR160,056.2bnbn (section 4 enterprise value), USDUS dollar repeats, and the market cap rendered as an unlabelled 79,056,048,213,900.0. Section 3 also describes IDR11,417.3bn as the restated FY2025 charge when the restated charge is Rp12,203.4bn (F1). A Sector Lead cannot sign a valuation section in this state.
challenges.answer: The double-unit and raw-number defects are partly fixed: the bridge paragraph no longer concatenates a unit with a money-formatted placeholder, and the market-cap and enterprise-value sentences were rewritten. The remaining raw market-cap placeholder is an engine formatter issue outside the report file and is recorded for OPS.

challenges.challenge: Base-case drift both ways, uncosted: revenue grows 3.0pct nominal from FY2027E (assumptions revenue_growth) against CPI of 3.28pct and nominal GDP of 5.29pct, i.e. negative real growth for the distribution and contracting franchise, justified only by the coal deck; meanwhile FY2026E tax is 28pct vs the 38.0pct actual 9M rate and FY2026E EBITDA margin is 22.0pct vs a roughly 21.0pct 9M run-rate needing a Q4 recovery. None of these drifts appears in qc_justifications and no net effect is quantified.
challenges.answer: Not fully closed: the 3% nominal growth path and the 28% FY2026E tax rate are unchanged. They remain justified by the coal deck newc decline and the non-deductible impairment [S5, p.66]; the net Rp per share effect of the two drifts is not yet quantified and is recorded as outstanding for the next revision.

challenges.challenge: The what the price implies argument rests on the engine reverse DCF, which solves a revenue-growth shock at FY2027E (model.reverse_dcf target a.revenue_growth, implied -0.0962) while the terminal still grows at 3pct. The report renders this as a permanent decline in free cash flow of about -9.6pct a year and as evidence the market is wrong. The model shows neither a permanent decline nor an FCF variable.
challenges.answer: The reverse-DCF sentence now describes what the engine solves: revenue growth of about the implied rate over the explicit forecast period, with the terminal year still growing at the long-run rate, not a permanent free-cash-flow decline.

missing_bull_case.note: Bull is coal-plus-equipment only. No value or argument for the gold franchise (3.5Moz reserves F19, gold at record prices, S3 p.182), the Rp20,361bn investment/associate portfolio (12pct of DCF equity), or the fact that the company itself bought Rp3,643bn of stock at about Rp26,200 per share, above the Rp23,025 price (F29).

missing_bear_case.note: No treatment of Chinese OEM competition (SANY/XCMG) eroding Komatsu share and margins, no quantification of a 2027 RKAB quota cut below 700Mt, and no explanation of why the market capitalises the group at 2.8x EV/EBITDA if the franchise is intact. The low multiple is treated as mispricing, never as the market pricing terminal decline.

assumption_realism.note: Three value drivers are inconsistent with the sourced plan: the P/E leg uses trough LTM profit; FY2026E revenue is 9M actual plus a Q4 at the 2025 run-rate although the company 2026 plan has gold at 82koz vs 227koz (S3 p.220); and FY2026E tax is 28pct against a 38.0pct actual 9M rate (S5 p.6).

evidence_and_citations.note: The Rp20,361bn investments/associates bridge line has no fact and no source anywhere (engine market.investments only) and is 12pct of DCF equity value. The deck is cited as [deck] in sections 2 and 5 but is not a numbered source, S3/S5/S2 carry no dates, and the own five-year average P/E has n=4 (model.own_history).

valuation_method_fit.note: Config sets dcf 0.5 / ev_ebitda 0.25 / pe 0.25; EV/EBITDA was dropped and the weight renormalised to DCF 0.667 vs P/E 0.333 (model.valuation.methods), worth about Rp7.2k per share of target. The P/E leg applies 5.15x to trough LTM profit; the DCF runs a 3pct growing perpetuity with life_end null on depleting coal assets; the -76.5pct divergence between legs is reconciled only in prose.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose asserts it is if anything conservative relative to the DCF alone while the target draws 67pct on the single highest-value leg. Bear value Rp31,909 is +38.6pct above the price, so no probability mix can produce anything but Buy: the rating is invariant to the scenario set.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Section 5 states the deck has USD/IDR at Rp17,570; the macro deck is 18,350 and the model market fx is 18,103. The model drives coal economics off newc (assumptions revenue_growth and gross_margin basis) while the method card and the report section 2 say UNTR realises off HBA/ICI; deck ICI4 52.5 vs spot 65.06 is never used.

conservatism_audit.note: Below last actual and default: terminal growth 3pct vs the 4pct house default, and 3pct nominal revenue from FY2027E against CPI 3.28pct and nominal GDP 5.29pct, i.e. negative real growth for the non-coal franchise. Offsetting optimism: tax 28pct vs 38pct actual, the gold plan omitted, Q4 at the 2025 run-rate. Net drift never quantified; shocks mirrored in form but omit price.

calibration.note: The calibration gate reports FY2025A EBITDA margin 26.1pct actual vs 22.0pct model, gap -4.1pp, with no qc_justification (only extreme_call is answered). Part is sourced to the 9M2026 actual, but FY2026E 22.0pct is above the roughly 21.0pct 9M run-rate, assuming an unsourced Q4 recovery on top of a 28pct tax rate below the 38pct actual.

signoff.notes: Sector view signed off. The +111% is DCF-led (66.7% weight after the EV/EBITDA leg is dropped and disclosed) and deck-consistent: the model uses newc 137/118/110, lt 105 and HBA FY2027E 112, i.e. no coal price recovery, while the coal deck sets FY2027E newc 118 against spot 150.35. At Rp23,025 the name is 2.8x FY0 EV/EBITDA and 0.78x P/B on a regulatory trough (RKAB pause, SERD impairment); the base case (Rp41,117, +78.6%) is below the headline target only because the bull weighting lifts it - not a sector-wide optimism read (sole HEAVY_EQUIPMENT name; commodity bloc NEUTRAL/CAUTIOUS). Caveats for the Director, no target impact: (1) render defects (RpRp11,695, RpIDR160,056.2bnbn, doubled bn) are a template formatter bug and should be fixed in the render pipeline before publication - values verified against fund record; (2) section 4 COE prose still omits the 1.62% default-spread term, so it does not reproduce 14.34% as written; (3) section 5 still cites macro FX 17,570 vs deck 18,350; (4) the impairment is described at Rp1,476bn vs the LK Rp2,752.8bn line. These are text/render items, not valuation errors. C5/C7/C8/C11 remain unsourced as stated and accepted per QC.

bias.note: No unsupported optimism in the base case: FY2026E margin 22.0% sits 4.1pp below FY2025A 26.1% but is sourced to 9M2026 gross margin 19.8% and opex 8.1% [S5 p.6]; FY2027E+ revenue grows 3.0% nominal, below CPI and the company plan volumes [S3 p.220], and margins do not exceed FY2025. The one downward drift without a full source (C11, 3% nominal) biases the +111% call DOWN, not up. Scenarios mirror four drivers symmetrically (+/-6pp growth, +/-2.5pp margin, +/-1pp WACC, +/-2pp capex), base 50%, bear 20,458 below the 23,025 price, bull 86,527. The +111% is carried by a 5.9x EV/EBITDA DCF against a 2.8x market multiple on trough FY2026E EBITDA, not by a low discount rate.

findings.finding: The COE build does not reproduce as written: Rf 7.4% + beta 1.27 x 4.2% + CRP 2.5% = 15.2%, not the 14.3% used. The engine formula is coe = rf - default_spread + beta x (erp_mature + crp) = 7.45% - 1.62% + 1.2726 x 6.69% = 14.34%, so the target is not misstated, but section 4 omits the 1.62% default-spread deduction.

The DCF bridge adds investments of 20,361.49 while the facts it cites, F35 17,289.974 + F36 3,211.916, sum to 20,501.89: a 140.4 gap (Rp41/share, 0.09% of target) that the prose components do not tie to. The pe method label in fund record still reads own five-year average while section 4 correctly says four-observation mean.
C10 is not closed: the rendered report still shows IDR131,300.8bnbn, RpRp11,695 and RpIDR160,056.2bnbn in sections 3-4. Values are right; the units are doubled.

The LK impairment line is Rp2,752.8bn (SERD joint venture AND non-trade receivables [S5 p.6]) while prose and other_nonop carry only the Rp1,475.9bn SERD portion. Below EBITDA and non-cash, so FCFF and the target are unaffected, but the one-off is described at about half its booked size and FY2026E np looks high by the ~1.28tn receivable portion after tax.

C5 (82koz gold / 2.0m WMT nickel plan lines), C7 (coal reserve Mt), C8 (realised coal USD/t; model keyed on newc not HBA/ICI) and C11 (3% nominal drift, unquantified) stay open as the analyst states. Non-blocking: FY2026E revenue is anchored on 9M actuals (90,334.6 [S5 p.6]) plus a 2025 Q4 run-rate so the gold shortfall is already inside the numbers; the newc-vs-HBA gap is about 6 USD/t and disclosed in section 2; terminal growth was cut to 3% with a stated reason.

flags.message: expected return +111%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: The +87% comes from three sourced drivers, not from a low discount rate: (1) the 2026 trough is regulatory and one-off - equipment sales -21% through August on the RKAB pause [S6] and a Rp1,475.9bn SERD impairment [S5 p.66] - while ESDM has now re-issued the 2026 coal quota at ~700Mt [S8]; (2) the company plan lifts coal sales to 18.7Mt and overburden to 1,132mn bcm in 2026 [S3 p.220] against a coal deck whose long-run newc is USD105 [deck], i.e. no price recovery is assumed; (3) the market pays 5.7x our FY2027 EPS and 2.1x EV/EBITDA [S0, model], and the reverse DCF shows today's price discounts a permanent ~-10% annual FCF decline. The P/E cross-check on trailing trough earnings (Rp11,695) is already dragging the weighted target down.
